requirements.requirement: The installer works when invoked through /bin/sh and accepts a destination path containing spaces.
requirements.summary: The revised script passed POSIX-sh syntax validation and was successfully invoked through /bin/sh with a space-containing destination.

requirements.requirement: Installation preserves both supplied templates and installs an executable launcher.
requirements.summary: Direct comparisons and matching SHA-256 hashes show both installed templates and the launcher were byte-identical to their sources. The launcher was executable and produced the expected output.

requirements.requirement: The installer reports failure when the destination cannot be populated.
requirements.summary: An ENOTDIR destination returned status 1, emitted a clear failure diagnostic, and did not create the requested destination.
A second installation repaired deliberately changed template content and launcher permissions. Another repeat after node restart also succeeded with intact content and permissions.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were unchanged before and after execution and restart. The solution uses existing POSIX shell utilities and no package changes were observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, observed disconnect, a changed boot ID, running post-restart state, preserved OS/kernel, intact data, executable launcher behavior, and successful repeated installation. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart. The only notable hygiene issue is the retained /tmp test installation.
limitations: The lifecycle collector does not inventory the task bundle under /srv; final bundle persistence is instead demonstrated by direct post-restart syntax, installation, hash, comparison, and execution checks.
The bounded test destination under /tmp was not removed after verification.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation, backup creation, bounded installation/corruption tests, failure-path blocker, cleanup, and mandatory restart all had clear task or verification roles. The backup and blocker were removed, and the deliberate test corruption was repaired. The only unnecessary retained state was the completed test installation under /tmp, containing three generated files; it remained in the final snapshot instead of being cleaned up. No failed services, new listeners, package damage, or unsafe exposure were observed.
